claims.claim: The standard Israeli VAT rate is 18 percent and exports of goods are zero-rated (0 percent).
claims.raw_snippet: The 2025 current rate of VAT is 18%. Exports of goods and certain services and various other transactions are zero-rated, and certain transactions are exempt.

claims.claim: Zero VAT on exports is governed by Section 30 (סעיף 30) of the VAT Law; the rate is conditional on documentation. If proof is missing the Tax Authority can deny the zero rate and assess at 18 percent.

claims.claim: Incoterms 2020 consists of 11 three-letter trade terms.
claims.raw_snippet: Incoterms® rules are a set of eleven three-letter trade terms, reflecting business-to-business practice in contracts for the sale and purchase of goods.

claims.claim: For shipments up to 6000 euros total invoice value, any Israeli exporter may use an invoice declaration instead of a EUR.1.
claims.raw_snippet: any exporter, if the total value of the products does not exceed €6,000.

claims.claim: Under the 2012 PEM rules that Israel still applies, an EUR.1 (and invoice declaration) proof of origin is valid for 4 months from the date of issue. The revised PEM Convention extends this to 10 months but does not apply to Israeli exports.
claims.raw_snippet: The proof of origin is valid for a period of 4 months from the date of issue.

claims.claim: The revised PEM Convention entered into force on 1 January 2025; 2025 was a transition year during which the 2012 and 2023 rules ran in parallel, and from 1 January 2026 only the revised rules apply between the parties that ratified them. Israel has not ratified and stays on the 2012 rules.
claims.raw_snippet: marking a significant milestone in the lead-up to the entry into force of the Revised PEM Convention on 1 January 2025

claims.claim: EUR.1 movement certificates and invoice declarations made out in Israel must state the postal code and the name of the city, village or industrial zone where origin-conferring production took place.
claims.raw_snippet: EUR.1 and invoice declarations issued or made out in Israel should bear the postal code and the name of the city, village, or industrial zone where production conferring originating status has taken place

claims.claim: Goods produced in Israeli settlements in territories brought under Israeli administration since June 1967 are not entitled to preferential tariff treatment under the EU-Israel Association Agreement.
claims.raw_snippet: products produced in those settlements are not entitled to benefit from preferential tariff treatment under the EU-Israel Association Agreement

claims.claim: Since 16 May 2023, importers into the EU of products originating in Israel must declare code Y864 on the import declaration.
claims.raw_snippet: As from 16 May 2023, importers and economic operators involved in imports into the European Union of products originating in Israel, must declare the new code Y864 in box 44 of the import declaration

claims.claim: Under the US-Israel FTA, the cost or value of materials produced in the exporting party plus direct processing costs there must be at least 35 percent of the appraised value of the article; up to 15 percent may come from the other party.
claims.raw_snippet: not less than 35 percent of the appraised value of the article

claims.claim: Effective January 10, 2018, the hard-copy Green Form (Form A) is no longer required; exporters complete and sign the US Origin Invoice Declaration instead.
claims.raw_snippet: Effective January 10, 2018, U.S. exporters to Israel are no longer required to provide Israeli authorities a hard copy Certificate of Origin

claims.raw_snippet: Israel and Vietnam signed the free trade agreement on 24. July 2023 and the agreement came into force on 17 November 2024.

claims.claim: An Israeli tax invoice requires a Tax Authority allocation number (mispar haktzaa) for the buyer to deduct the input VAT; the threshold fell to 10,000 NIS on 1 January 2026 and to 5,000 NIS on 1 June 2026.

claims.claim: As of 27 July 2026 no suspension of EU-Israel trade preferences is in force: the September 2025 Commission proposal was never adopted by the Council, and subsequent Foreign Affairs Council discussions in April and July 2026 ended without a decision.
claims.raw_snippet: The legal basis for the EU's trade relations with Israel is the EU-Israel Association Agreement, which entered into force in June 2000.

claims.raw_snippet: alternative rules of origin apply until 31 December 2025. As of 1 January 2026, only the revised PEM Convention will apply

claims.claim: For imports into the United States from Israel, CBP eliminated the Form A certificate of origin on 20 May 1994 and replaced it with a signed affidavit requested from the importer; the 2017 amendment changed nothing for imports into the US. The 10 January 2018 date applies to US exports to Israel.
claims.raw_snippet: Effective May 20, 1994, the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) eliminated the requirement for importers to submit the certificate of origin

claims.claim: Under section 22(a) of the Israeli VAT Law the tax point for a sale of goods is delivery to the buyer, regardless of when payment is received; section 22(b) applies a cash basis to a dealer whose turnover does not exceed 2 million NIS and certain other categories.
